expectations.text: The skill discovers and reads the existing rules file before writing anything
expectations.evidence: Transcript Step 1: 'Read the input file at .claude/skills/rule-creator/evals/fixtures/new-rule-creation/.claude/rules/team-standards.md. Found an existing file with Code Style, Debugging, and Testing sections.'

expectations.text: It asks which section the rule belongs in (or suggests Code Style)
expectations.evidence: Transcript Step 2: 'Identified the right location for the new rule. The Debugging section was the natural home since it already referenced console.* usage.' It suggests Debugging rather than Code Style, which is reasonable.

expectations.text: The rule text is one clear imperative sentence, not a paragraph or multi-sentence explanation
expectations.evidence: Output file shows a multi-sentence rule: 'Do not commit console.log, console.debug, console.info, or console.warn statements used for debugging. Remove all temporary console logging before committing code. If a console call is intentional (e.g., inside a logger utility or error boundary), add a comment eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- <reason> to document why it must stay.' This is 3 sentences, not 1.

expectations.text: The rule is classified as T1 (console.log has a clear syntactic signature)
expectations.evidence: The output uses an HTML comment enforcement block (<!-- ENFORCEMENT ... -->) with no tier classification at all. The block contains 'detection: grep for console.(log|debug|info|warn)' which implies tool-enforceable, but no explicit T1 classification.

expectations.text: The enforcement block has a regex pattern matching console.log
expectations.evidence: Output enforcement block contains: 'detection: grep for console\.(log|debug|info|warn)' -- a regex pattern matching console.log and variants.

expectations.text: The rule is appended to an appropriate section, not dumped at the end of the file
expectations.evidence: Output file shows the new rule under '## Debugging' section, after the existing logger utility rule and before '## Testing'. The enforcement block follows the rule within the Debugging section.

expectations.text: Budget checks run after generating the block
expectations.evidence: The transcript and output contain no budget check or budget reporting. The without_skill run does not track enforcement block budgets at all.

claims.claim: The enforcement block includes exceptions for eslint-disable comments
claims.evidence: Output enforcement block: 'exceptions: lines with an explicit eslint-disable comment that includes a reason'. This is a reasonable escape hatch.

eval_feedback.overall: The without_skill run produces reasonable content but misses the tier classification system, budget tracking, and concise rule writing -- key skill differentiators.
